one_liner: CivicState is built, but Brooks History stays watchlist until the operator confirms the business identity.

authority.quorum: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption - operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record
authority.decisionRecord: Pending operator merge; this worker cannot approve the plan.
authority.rationale: The soul is refreshed but remains needs-revision because the registry identity says personal/research watchlist while the repo implements CivicState.

pomReviews.summary: Prepared a conditional business plan and gate; operator identity confirmation is required before roadmap authority.

research.summary: Workspace-only EIR pass. Evidence came from repo planning docs, source files, package metadata, and the dispatch registry note. No network research was performed; external market claims are marked as assumptions.
methods: Read existing soul/planning artifacts and preserved true CivicState content.
Inspected app source shape to distinguish implemented surfaces from roadmap claims.
Built bottom-up market and financial models from paid jobs and prior repo assumptions.
Applied anti-plan scrutiny to identity mismatch, demand, deliverability, legal-adjacent risk, and moat weakness.

planningMethod.evidenceHarvest: Harvested repo-local evidence from planning docs, source files, package metadata, and the dispatch registry note.
planningMethod.marketResearch: No network; all external market sizing is assumption-labeled and bottom-up from paid job counts.
planningMethod.financialValidation: Reconciled revenue as paid submissions times average order value and carried prior cost/margin assumptions with labels.
planningMethod.alternativeSearch: Compared standalone CivicState venture, research/archive posture, and WrkPlug client posture.
planningMethod.antiPlan: Attacked the plan for identity mismatch, unproven demand, deliverability failure, compliance risk, and nonexistent launch moat.
planningMethod.finalSynthesis: Create a conditional soul that blocks roadmap authority until operator identity confirmation and market tests.

segments.name: US residents with a specific civic issue
segments.painfulJob: They want government action but need help identifying officials, finding citations, drafting credible letters, and sending them.

segments.name: Future HOAs, nonprofits, and civic organizations
segments.painfulJob: They may need repeatable civic outreach workflows, but this remains deferred until individual usage is proven.

currentSubstitutes: Enterprise advocacy tools such as Quorum and VoterVoice.
willingnessToPayEvidence: Repo plan sets $5, $15, and $25 one-time packages.
No workspace evidence of actual paid transactions.
Payment willingness remains an assumption until beta conversion is measured.

market.category: AI-assisted civic letter drafting, official routing, and delivery.
market.competitiveLandscape: Free direct outreach, Resistbot, Change.org, LegalZoom-style drafting, and enterprise advocacy platforms all solve pieces of the job.
market.wedge: Start with individual paid civic letters; only expand if paid conversion, official coverage, citation reliability, and deliverability clear gates.

businessModel.valueCreation: Compress civic research, official targeting, citation-backed drafting, and email delivery into one paid workflow.
businessModel.valueDelivery: Next.js web app, Express API, BullMQ/OpenClaw workers, Prisma data model, Stripe, Postmark, Clerk, and legal/citation modules currently exist in source.
businessModel.pricing: $5 single, $15 three-pack, $25 full-spread based on repo planning artifacts.
businessModel.revenuePath: Beta paid submissions first, SEO/public campaign pages second, organization/API revenue only after individual pipeline proof.
businessModel.unitEconomics: Prior model shows $15 package with $1.20 total COGS, $13.80 gross profit, and 92% margin; unvalidated until live costs are measured.
businessModel.operatingCosts: Model tokens, Stripe fees, Postmark delivery, hosting, local officials data provider, moderation, compliance review, and operator time.
businessModel.marginLogic: Low direct delivery and token costs may support high margin, but moderation, refunds, deliverability, and legal review can erase the apparent margin.

financialModel.summary: Base model is conditional and reconciles as submissions times average order value. 2027 base revenue is $86,400 from 4,800 submissions at $18 AOV.
financialModel.validationStatus: Needs operator and market validation; not approved for roadmap authority.
revenueAssumptions: Average order value starts at $15 and reaches $20 by month 24 per repo model.
Paid submissions reach 400 per month by month 12 only if SEO or referral distribution works.
No organization API or subscription revenue is included before operator validation.
costAssumptions: Variable costs remain 12% of revenue based on the prior break-even model.
Fixed operating costs start near $200 per month but rise with support, data, and compliance needs.
Human review costs increase with flagged content and legal-adjacent submissions.
sensitivityTests: If conversion is 1% instead of the prior >=3% gate, revenue misses the base model.
If .gov inbox placement is below the prior >=85% gate, refunds and churn may overwhelm margin.
If local official coverage is below the prior >=60% gate, local SEO and neighborhood use cases weaken.

alternatives.name: Standalone CivicState venture
alternatives.thesis: The implemented app can become a paid civic-letter tool for individuals.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Low price point and high modeled gross margin if conversion and delivery work.
alternatives.financialCase: $86,400 annual base revenue at 4,800 submissions and $18 AOV.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Selected only conditionally; identity and market gates remain open.

alternatives.name: Brooks History as research/archive asset
alternatives.thesis: The registry may intend this repo to be personal/research rather than an investible business.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Avoids misleading portfolio claims and preserves source value.
alternatives.financialCase: $0 near-term investible value until operator confirms business posture.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Kept as the default watchlist posture from the dispatch registry note.

alternatives.name: WrkPlug client app
alternatives.thesis: CivicState could consume shared auth, billing, identity, and account rails instead of owning them.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Lower duplicated infrastructure and shared-rails compounding.
alternatives.financialCase: Potential cost and CAC savings remain unvalidated because WrkPlug Phase 0 is not signed.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Selected as platform posture guidance, not build authority.

antiPlan.summary: The deal should be killed or paused if the identity mismatch persists, users do not pay, official emails do not land, citations cannot be trusted, or compliance review makes the unit economics fake.

holes.hole: The repo identity may be wrong.
holes.whyItMatters: A VC-grade plan for CivicState is misleading if Brooks History is only a personal/research asset.
holes.repair: Require operator ruling before investor-facing positioning or roadmap scale.

holes.whyItMatters: A $5-$25 price point still fails if users expect civic tools to be free.
holes.repair: Run beta conversion tests before adding features.

holes.whyItMatters: The paid job is delivery to officials; filtered email destroys value.
holes.repair: Treat .gov inbox placement, bounce rates, and complaint suppression as launch gates.

holes.hole: Legal-adjacent citation risk can swamp the business.
holes.whyItMatters: Bad citations or legal-demand framing can create reputational, compliance, or legal exposure.
holes.repair: Keep citation verification, disclaimers, moderation, and human review as hard gates.

mitigations: WrkPlug posture review before further standalone platform investment.
residualRisks: Operator may confirm the asset is not investible.
Organic SEO may not convert to paid submissions.
Moderation and compliance workload may break the one-operator model.
Incumbents may copy the workflow before the data moat compounds.

strategy.diagnosis: There is more implementation than business proof, and the repo identity conflicts with the registry.
strategy.guidingPolicy: Do not scale or pitch until identity, demand, deliverability, and citation gates are proven.
strategy.whereToPlay: Individual US resident civic issues, if operator confirms CivicState is the intended asset.
strategy.howToWin: Own the full workflow from issue to researched, citation-backed, delivered official letter at a low one-time price.
strategy.moatHypothesis: Officials data, citation verification history, delivery outcomes, and public campaign pages compound only after real volume.
coherentActions: Audit official lookup and citation verification.
tradeoffs: Do not market as near-term investible while registry watchlist remains unresolved.
Do not add broad community features before paid delivery works.
Do not treat prior financial projections as evidence of demand.
Do not hard-wire standalone platform rails if WrkPlug becomes authoritative.

channels: Opt-in public campaign pages for SEO after privacy review.
Direct outreach to civic communities after deliverability proof.
assumptions: Users will pay for done-for-you research and routing.
Public campaign pages can create acquisition without creating moderation overload.
WrkPlug shared rails may reduce CAC, but this is not signed.

jobs: Approve compliance posture before real sends.
Track conversion, revenue, refunds, and support burden.

regulatory: Treat CAN-SPAM, CCPA/GDPR, AI disclosure, and moderation requirements as repo-planned constraints, not legal conclusions.
privacy: Political opinions and civic complaints are sensitive user data.
The Prisma model marks full name, issue description, desired outcome, and letter content for app-level encryption.
security: Use least-privilege credentials for Stripe, Postmark, Clerk, Anthropic, and data providers.
Append-only ledger and audit logs require HMAC tamper detection per repo schema.
brand: No legal-demand, harassment, or defamation framing.
operational: No scale before operator identity ruling.
No official sends before deliverability and moderation gates.
No organization/API expansion before individual pipeline proof.

successMetrics: Citation audit passes without fabricated citations.
killTriggers: Operator confirms this is only a research asset.
Paid conversion remains below viable threshold after beta.
Deliverability cannot reach the prior gate.
Citation verification fails on real issue samples.
pivotTriggers: Users want free drafting but not paid delivery.
Organizations show stronger willingness to pay than individuals.
reviseTriggers: Live cost data invalidates the 92% margin model.
Compliance review changes allowable delivery or messaging.

aiWorkGovernance.wedge: Use AI for research, classification, drafting, delivery preparation, and treasury logging under audit and human-review gates.
aiWorkGovernance.problem: AI-generated civic correspondence can fabricate citations, misroute officials, or create legal-adjacent risk if ungated.
aiWorkGovernance.promise: Every AI output must be source-linked, citation-verified, moderated, and auditable before delivery.
duplicatePrevention: Tie roadmap work to BUSINESS.md headings.
Route identity and platform-posture conflicts back before implementation.
Keep organization/API expansion out of scope until individual proof exists.
coordinationMetrics: Roadmap items trace to business headings.
Operator identity ruling captured before scale.
tokenSpendControls: Do not spend worker effort on new feature scope until identity is resolved.
Use audits and tabletop tests before live delivery.
Measure model cost per submission against the unit model.
aiWorkGovernance.risk: Over-automation can create legal-adjacent harm; under-automation can make the product uneconomic.
